answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it can transact, the way a wharf charges a berthing fee before a boat can dock. Fake identities then cost real capital, so flooding the network stops paying. Stake is slashed when peers attest to fraud, and reputation flows downstream like a river: trust earned by one identity cannot be duplicated for free. An attacker who burns stake on fakes ends at the nadir of the trust graph, isolated and unable to borrow anyone else's credibility.
